tasks.short: Assign cataloguing and maintenance work, track loans, chase overdue items, plan repairs, handle teachers' requests and meet staff.

steps.what: Coordinator assigns cataloging and maintenance work to library and lab staff
Coordinator tracks loans of materials and equipment in a spreadsheet
Coordinator reviews the overdue list each week
Coordinator chases overdue loans by e-mail
Coordinator reviews equipment condition reports and plans repairs
Coordinator answers teachers' requests for educational materials
Coordinator meets staff about problems in the library and labs

tasks.design: A loan system ({OTHER}) with barcodes records check-out and return, sends reminders for overdue items, and keeps condition reports per item. Teachers search the online catalogue and reserve materials themselves, so fewer requests reach the coordinator by e-mail. Assigning work, planning repairs and meeting staff stay with the coordinator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loans were kept in a spreadsheet and chased by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Loan systems handle barcode check-out, reservations and reminders.
tasks.still_hard: Teachers return late anyway; some items need a personal ask.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which teacher needs the microscopes before the exam week.

reach.learn: Whether barcode loans cut missing equipment.

evidence.claim: Loan systems handle barcode check-out, reservations and overdue reminders.

assumptions: Boundary: from assigning work to resolved problems; buying materials is outside.
Input contract: catalogue records entered by library staff; fallback is the spreadsheet.
Assigning, planning repairs and meetings do not change.
Library staff time is outside the coordinator's savings.

incremental.description: Coordinator sets up loan rules once.

approvals.approved_version: The overdue list as checked by the coordinator that week.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review learner levels with teachers, adapt texts and tasks per level, choose delivery methods, agree the materials and publish them.

steps.what: Coordinator reviews learner groups' levels and needs with teachers
Coordinator adapts instructional content for different levels of learners

loop.input: The source text or task, the target level descriptors and the learning objectives; no learner data.
loop.output: Adapted versions per level with word lists.
loop.check: Code checks length and word-list limits per level and that every learning objective tag is still covered; the coordinator reviews each version for accuracy and fit.
loop.stop: One draft per level; on failure the coordinator adapts by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rewriting a text for a lower reading level needs language generation; templates cannot do it.

steps.what: Coordinator chooses delivery methods per group
Coordinator agrees the adapted materials with teachers and adjusts them
Coordinator formats and uploads the materials to the learning platform

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts adapted versions of a text or task per level from the source, the level descriptors and the objectives, with no learner data; code checks length, word lists and objective coverage, and the coordinator reviews every version. After the coordinator and teachers agree the final set, it is published to the learning platform ({LMS}) in the house layout. Reviewing needs, choosing methods and agreeing with teachers stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each level version was rewritten by hand and formatted per course.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson tools rewrite text by level, and a trial found AI help cut lesson preparation time.
tasks.still_hard: Simplified text can lose meaning; the coordinator must check every version.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what a struggling group will find too childish.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator reviews drafted versions instead of writing each one.

reach.learn: Whether teachers use the adapted versions.

evidence.claim: LessonUp rewrites slide text by tone or level, translates and makes word lists.
In a randomised trial in England, teachers using an AI lesson assistant spent 49 minutes less a week on lesson preparation, with quality no worse.
Schools must keep personal data out of AI tools, sign a processor agreement and do a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from level needs to published materials; teaching the lesson is outside.
Input contract: group results from the teachers; level descriptors set by the curriculum team; fallback is rewriting by hand.
Reviewing needs, choosing methods and agreeing do not change.
Teachers' time is outside the coordinator's savings.
research_questions: Do weaker groups do better with adapted versions?

incremental.description: Coordinator keeps level descriptors and word lists current.

approvals.approved_version: The materials as agreed and adjusted by the coordinator in s4; later edits need a new agreement before publishing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Subjects with technical terms need more checking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Export results, combine them, compute course and item statistics, interpret what works and write the evaluation report.

steps.what: Coordinator exports results from the learning platform and student system
Coordinator combines performance data in a spreadsheet
Coordinator computes pass rates and item statistics
Coordinator analyzes the data to determine effectiveness of courses and materials
Coordinator writes the evaluation report

tasks.design: Results flow from the learning platform ({LMS}) and student system into a dashboard ({BI}) with pass rates, item difficulty and trends per course and material, at group level. The coordinator interprets the findings and writes the report using the dashboard's charts. No AI judges courses or learners.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were exported and combined in spreadsheets each term.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning platforms export results, and test tools run item analysis.
tasks.still_hard: Numbers show where results drop, not why.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a drop comes from a new teacher, not the material.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator interprets a dashboard instead of building spreadsheets.

evidence.claim: Digital assessment platforms can grade closed questions automatically and run item analysis.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk; this design uses group statistics without AI.
Using pupil data needs the parent or pupil section of the participation council to agree.

assumptions: Boundary: from course results to the evaluation report; changing courses is outside.
Input contract: results recorded by teachers in the learning platform and student system; fallback is spreadsheet exports.
Interpreting and reporting stay with the coordinator.
Groups smaller than ten are not shown.
research_questions: Do courses change after the dashboard shows weak items?

incremental.description: Coordinator checks dashboard figures against a sample of raw results.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Courses with results outside the platform save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set survey questions, send surveys, sort free-text comments into themes, observe lessons, talk with teachers and learners and write recommendations.

steps.what: Coordinator sets the survey questions for the course
Coordinator e-mails survey links to learners
Coordinator reads learners' free-text comments on satisfaction and technology use

loop.output: Themes with counts and two or three example quotes each.
loop.check: Code checks every quote occurs in the input and that no theme is shown for groups under ten respondents; the coordinator reads a random sample of comments against the themes.
loop.stop: One run per survey; if the sample disagrees, the coordinator reads all comments.
loop.why_not_simpler: Comments vary in wording; word counts miss what learners mean.

steps.what: Coordinator observes lessons and the use of instructional technology
Coordinator talks with teachers and learners about knowledge transfer and what works
Coordinator writes recommendations to improve instruction

tasks.design: Once the coordinator has set the questions, the learning platform ({LMS}) sends the survey to learners at course end. A bounded step sorts free-text comments into themes with quoted examples, at group level only, and the coordinator reads a sample to check them. Observing lessons, talking with teachers and learners and writing recommendations stay with the coordinator; no emotion or behaviour analysis is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Surveys were sent by hand and every comment read and sorted in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning platforms send surveys, and language models can group comments into themes with quotes.
tasks.still_hard: Themes flatten nuance; a single serious comment can get lost.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing in a lesson why learners say the tool is hard to use.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator checks comment themes instead of sorting every comment.

reach.learn: Whether themed comments lead to changes.

evidence.claim: Language models can group free-text comments into themes with example quotes.
Emotion recognition in education is banned; this design reads written comments at group level only.

assumptions: Boundary: from survey design to recommendations; course changes are outside.
Input contract: course design from the curriculum team; survey answers from learners, without names; fallback is reading all comments.
Observing, talking and recommending do not change.
research_questions: How often does the sample disagree with the themes?

already_counted.description: Coordinator reads a sample of comments against the themes.

incremental.description: Coordinator sets survey timing in the platform.

approvals.approved_version: The survey questions as set by the coordinator in s1; changed questions need a new setting before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is observing and talking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The instructional coordinator keeps judging what works and agreeing with teachers; spreadsheets, rewrites and comment sorting shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A coordinator who spends saved time in classrooms instead of in spreadsheets.
